summary: branching.plan(n, root, edges) returns the cheapest acyclic set of upstream edges that reaches every node from the source, as the ascending original edge indices, or None when impossible.

cores.name: branching.plan

contract.inputs: n in [1, 1000]; root in [0, n-1]; edges = up to 20000 triples (u, v, cost) with |cost| <= 10^12 integers; negative costs, self-loops, parallel edges allowed; inputs are never mutated
contract.outputs: (minimum_total_cost, ascending list of selected original edge indices) or None; n == 1 -> (0, []); the source has no incoming edge and every other node exactly one; selected edges are acyclic and reach every node from root
contract.complexity: O(n * (n + len(edges))) worst case; at most n-1 contraction rounds; no subset enumeration and no per-node independent cheapest-edge choice

cores.algorithm: Chu-Liu/Edmonds minimum arborescence with group-level edge sets, cycle detection on the selected-incoming-edge functional graph, cycle contraction with the incoming discount, and iterative expansion back to original edges
cores.statistics_hook: branching._solve(n, root, edges) returns (result, stats) with stats = {rounds, cycles, levels, lookups}; only used for reporting

independent_oracles.name: brute_force
independent_oracles.method: enumerates every combination of incoming edges for all non-source nodes and keeps the cheapest acyclic selection that reaches every node

independent_oracles.name: reference_cost
independent_oracles.method: separately written cost-only recursive textbook Edmonds contraction with fresh node ids each round; shares no bookkeeping with branching.py

independent_oracles.name: TestBruteForceCrossCheck
independent_oracles.method: its own exhaustive enumeration helper, independent of verify.py

last_run_summary.differential_small: 12000 random graphs, 12000 exhaustive-optimum comparisons, 0 mismatches, 0 structurally invalid
last_run_summary.differential_larger: 6000 random graphs up to n=9/m=16, 1575 exhaustive comparisons, 0 mismatches, 0 structurally invalid
last_run_summary.reference_medium: 1000 random graphs with 2 <= n <= 60 and up to 250 edges, 0 mismatches against the independent recursive oracle
last_run_summary.traceability: all 6 demo scenarios trace every node back to the source through original input edges
last_run_summary.scale: n=1000, m=20000 at the documented maximum, all results structurally valid

what_is_actually_checked: optimal total cost equal to an independent exhaustive/reference optimum
None exactly when no rooted branching exists
selected indices ascending, unique, and within range
exactly n-1 selected edges; source has no incoming edge; every other node has exactly one
selected edges are acyclic (supplied by the one-incoming-edge plus reachability checks) and every node is reachable from the source
reported total equals the sum of the original costs of the selected edges
input edges are not modified; tuple inputs accepted
traceability: each node's path through the selected original edges terminates at the source
not_claimed: no claim of matching any specific tie-breaking between multiple optimal solutions; ties resolve deterministically on the original edge index
no claim about behavior outside the documented input bounds

scale_facts.case: sequential contraction cascade (worst case, one merge per round)

real_verification.note: timings are wall-clock on the current machine and illustrative only; the measured growth of t/(n*(n+m)) stays roughly constant across n, consistent with the claimed bound

covers: negative costs where the more expensive cycle entry wins
entries into a cycle from inside and from outside
multi-level contraction (3 nested rounds, expansion depth 3)
self-loops and parallel edges never corrupting the plan
demos.output_style: per scenario: original edge list, selected original edges with indices and costs, per-node path of original edges to the source with path cost, structural audit, and an exhaustive brute-force cross-check where the graph is small

demos.covers: same scenarios without the large scale measurements
15 curated tests: spec examples, negative costs, cycle entries, nested contraction, self-loops, parallel edges, unreachable, input immutability, brute-force cross-check, maximum-size scale runs

limits.language: Python 3 standard library only; no third-party packages
limits.memory: O(n + len(edges)) working state plus per-contraction group metadata, bounded by the number of contracted cycles
limits.determinism: identical input yields identical output (ties break on the smallest original edge index)
